🇲🇽📈 <u>Analysts: Mexico keeps growing, inflation eases — no recession</u>

Private-sector analysts in Citi's expectations survey see Mexico's economy growing 1.8% in 2027 with inflation cooling to 3.8%, and they nudged the 2026 growth forecast up to 1.3% — a steady, no-recession outlook even with Trump's tariffs looming, El Financiero reports.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Most Mexicans want no US troops on their soil</u>

As Washington floats "unilateral" strikes on cartels, a recent El Soberano poll finds 55% of Mexicans reject US military operations inside Mexico. It tracks President Sheinbaum's line — cooperation yes, subordination never — and a deeper reflex on the very week Mexico marks the Niños Héroes: the country that lost half its territory to a US invasion in 1847 isn't inviting the army back.

🇲🇽📉 <u>Zacatecas: daily homicides down 96% since 2021</u>

Once one of Mexico's bloodiest states, Zacatecas cut its daily homicide average 96% between 2021 and 2026 — from 4.5 killings a day to 0.2 — SESNSP chief Marcela Figueroa Franco reported. Measured just from the start of Sheinbaum's term (Sept 2024–Aug 2026) the drop is still 85%, from 1.13 to 0.17 a day. It's the lowest average in a series that reaches back to 2015.

🇲🇽💜 <u>Mexico City moves to pay for the invisible work that sustains life</u>

Women in CDMX spend up to 50 hours a week on unpaid care in the poorest households — against 14 for men — Mayor Clara Brugada said as she installed the city's Junta de Cuidados. Her program "Ciudad que Cuida a Quien Cuida" starts by paying 5,000 caregivers, most of them women, toward what she calls the "fourth R": remunerating the labor that keeps society alive — built on three aims, to desfeminize, desfamiliarize and desmercantilize care.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex isolates Gulf pipeline leak; ASEA confirms it's contained</u>

A crude leak detected 46 nautical miles off Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche was brought under control after Pemex depressurized and shut the marine gathering pipeline at the Cantarell field. ASEA — Mexico's oil-sector safety regulator — flew over the installations with the Navy and confirmed no crude is reaching the coast; specialized vessels keep collecting and dispersing hydrocarbons while repairs finish in the coming days.

🇲🇽✊ <u>Rarámuri self-rule is not a "bureaucratic simulation"</u>

In the Sierra Tarahumara, the Rarámuri siríami (traditional governors) of Norogachi told federal and state officials to respect their right to self-determination: social-infrastructure funds should be decided in community assembly, not spent on suppliers "recommended" by bureaucrats — often their own relatives. "The imposition of government tutelage stops our empowerment, reducing our autonomy to a bureaucratic simulation," they said, rejecting latrines nobody asked for while they build the capacity to run their own projects.
For the First Time in History, Every Indigenous Community Gets a Direct Budget

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>NO GASOLINAZO: PEMEX EATS 1,757 MILLION PESOS A MONTH TO PROTECT DRIVERS</u>

As the US–Iran war pushes Brent to 108 dollars, Mexican pump prices barely move. Pemex is absorbing 1,756.9 million pesos a month — 10,541 million since March — to hold regular gasoline under 24 pesos and diesel under 27, per PETROIntelligence via El Financiero. And it’s holding that line with a 3.43-peso IEPS subsidy on regular, versus 12.51 pesos during the 2022 shock: a quarter of the fiscal help, the same protection for families.

🇲🇽📚 <u>UNAM OWNS ITS MISTAKE: ADMISSION EXAMS GO BACK IN PERSON</u>

After its digital admission test failed, Mexico’s UNAM is returning to in-person exams — and its rector didn’t dodge it: “The University and its rector take responsibility for the failures and the errors.” Tests will run on pre-loaded devices across multiple sites, with a new AI council to steer the technology. A public university held to account by its own students, not by spin.
banner: UNAM: ADMISSION EXAMS RETURN IN PERSON

🔥🇲🇽 <u>WASHINGTON’S OWN FILES: TORTURE AND 26,121 DISAPPEARED UNDER CALDERÓN & PEÑA</u>

The same US that armed Calderón’s drug war quietly documented the results. A 2013 State Department human-rights report logged 7,000 unidentified bodies and 26,121 people disappeared between 2006 and 2012 — unlawful killings, torture and forced disappearances by Mexican security forces. This was the “partnership” era run by security chief Genaro García Luna, now convicted in a US court of taking Sinaloa Cartel bribes.
